$comment: Single source of truth for how CI splits the e2e suite: one shard per
microservice plus a 'core' shard for the core-hosted tests.
'paths' entries are passed verbatim to `playwright test`, which treats them as
REGEXES tested (unanchored, case-insensitive) against the ABSOLUTE spec path -
not as directory names. So they are anchored on both ends: a leading '/' pins
the segment boundary and a trailing '$' pins the extension. Without that,
a future tests/interview-v2/ would silently join the 'interview' shard.
Note: a pattern that both starts and ends with '/' would be parsed by
Playwright as a /regex/flags literal and lose its leading slash, which is why
directory patterns end in '.*\\.spec\\.ts$' rather than a bare '/'.
scripts/shards.mjs check asserts this covers every spec under tests/ exactly
once and that no pattern is stale; CI runs that check before any shard starts
and builds its matrix from this file, so adding a suite here is all it takes.
cacheWriter marks the single shard that exports the Docker layer cache. It
sits on the shard with the lightest test load so the extra export time stays
off the critical path; retune it if shard runtimes shift.
